seo_description: Free, open-source menu bar app for macOS. Copy many items in a row, then paste them back in order with one hotkey. Native, offline, no accounts.
hero_sub: PasteStackQueue turns on a copy queue with Control-Option-C, then pastes each item into the frontmost app in order with Control-Option-V. Free, native and offline.
features_sub: A small menu bar app that does multi-item copy and paste and nothing else.

features.title: Two global hotkeys
features.desc: Toggle queue mode with Control-Option-C and paste the next item with Control-Option-V. Both can be re-recorded in Settings, with a warning if a shortcut is unavailable.

features.title: FIFO, LIFO or paste all
features.desc: Paste oldest-first or newest-first, or paste the whole queue at once joined by a newline, comma, tab, space or semicolon.

features.title: Fill forms with auto-advance
features.desc: Optionally send a Tab keypress after each paste so values land in successive fields. Text, files and images can all be queued.

features.title: Menu bar queue you can edit
features.desc: See queued items with the next one marked by an arrow. Drag to reorder, delete single items or clear the queue. A brief HUD confirms each copy and paste.

features.title: Careful with sensitive data
features.desc: Concealed, transient and auto-generated pasteboard types such as password manager copies are ignored. Items over 1 MB are skipped and the queue is capped at 200.

features.title: Survives crashes and restarts
features.desc: The queue is mirrored to a small JSON file, and your original clipboard can be restored when the queue empties. Launch at login is optional.

permissions_step: When you first paste, grant Accessibility in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility so the app can send the Command-V keystroke.

faq.q: Is PasteStackQueue really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, with no accounts, no ads and no paid tier. The full source is on GitHub, and a donation link is there if you want to support development.

Only Accessibility, which is used to send Command-V (and the optional Tab) to the frontmost app. Without it, the paste hotkey still places the next item on your clipboard and you press Command-V yourself. The app has no network access.
Only on your Mac. While the queue has items, it is mirrored to a small JSON file in ~/Library/Application Support/PasteStackQueue/ so a crash does not lose it. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to launch it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
